clue.text: Flora's neat move

definitions.note: read as 'Flora is': a single plant of the flora, the 's being the link

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so one beast is a cow
to slip is to move quietly or smoothly

explanation.surface: Flora, a person, makes a tidy manoeuvre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flora' poses as a woman's name but is the plant life of a region, here one wild flower; 'neat' is not tidy but the old word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowslip is a yellow spring wildflower, one member of the countryside's plant life.

clue.text: The craft shown by many a forecaster

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many
an oracle foretells the future

explanation.surface: A vessel is shown on screen by plenty of TV weather presenters.
explanation.definitionFit: A coracle is a small round boat of wicker and hide, a traditional Welsh craft.

clue.text: Fly eccentric's screwy device

parts.note: to wing is to fly
a nut is a crank or eccentric; the 's reads as 'is' joining to the definition

explanation.surface: An odd person's fishing fly turns out to be a strange gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A wing nut is a nut with two flat lugs, turned by hand on a screw thread.

clue.text: A simpleton backing up a scrubber

indicators.note: in a down clue backing up means the letters run from bottom to top, so read backwards

parts.note: a fool is a simpleton

explanation.surface: A dim helper is supporting a cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing up' turns the whole of A FOOL, giving LOOFA.
explanation.definitionFit: A loofah is the dried fibrous gourd used as a bath sponge for scrubbing skin.

clue.text: Knocking off pop is a dastardly crime!

definitions.text: Knocking off pop is a dastardly crime!

parts.words: Knocking off pop is a dastardly crime!
parts.note: knocking off reads as killing and pop as one's father, so the crime is murdering a parent

explanation.surface: Stopping for a fizzy drink or ending the music is somehow wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: Killing one's own father is the crime with this Latin-derived name, from pater and -cide.

clue.text: Self-important pups moo for attention

indicators.note: the letters are worked over and given fresh attention, rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: Young dogs low like cows to be noticed, rather full of themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for attention' asks for PUPS MOO to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone pompous is puffed up and full of their own dignity.

clue.text: Class where the student must stay in step

indicators.note: the student letter has to stay within the word for step, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: a pace is a single step
L is the learner plate, a learner being a student

explanation.surface: A classroom where the pupil must keep up with the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: L comes from the British learner-driver plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Place means rank or standing, as in knowing one's place in the social order.

clue.text: They'll deter closet troublemakers

parts.note: closet troublemakers seem to be secret rebels, but are insects in the wardrobe that eat clothes

explanation.surface: Something will discourage hidden agitators.
explanation.definitionFit: Small balls of naphthalene are hung in wardrobes to keep fabric-eating insects off woollens.

clue.text: Scoffed more than was justified about a note

parts.note: over can mean about, as in a dispute over money
te is the seventh note of the tonic sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone mocked a musical note more than it deserved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoffed' looks like mocked but means ate greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: To overeat is to consume more food than one needs; scoffed is slang for gobbled.

clue.text: States page in school is not to be trusted

indicators.note: the pieces sit in the word for school, one placed inside another

parts.note: a sect is a school of thought or faith
US is the United States

explanation.surface: An American pageboy at school cannot be relied upon.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspect describes something doubtful or questionable, inviting distrust.

clue.text: To make a lot of noise is right in disorder

definitions.text: To make a lot of noise

parts.note: gout is a painful disorder of the joints

explanation.surface: Being correct amid chaos makes a racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in disorder' looks like an anagram signal, but IN is kept and the disorder is the illness GOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Bells ring out when they peal loudly, filling the air with sound.

clue.text: The man's composed some music

indicators.note: composed suggests putting notes together, here putting the letters into a fresh order

parts.note: taken letter by letter, including the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: A man has written some songs.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthems are songs of praise or national hymns, pieces of music.

clue.text: Singing of a worker going in a taxi to the Italian quarter

indicators.note: the worker goes into the taxi, one word placed within another

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
an ant is the crossword's standard worker
il is the Italian for the
E, east, is one quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: A labourer takes a cab to the Italian district.
explanation.definitionFit: Cantabile is a musical direction meaning in a smooth, songlike style.

clue.text: Support for a couple

explanation.surface: Something holds up two people.
explanation.definitionFit: A brace is a strut or prop giving support, and also a pair, as in a brace of pheasants.

clue.text: The person having a meal in a new cafe-a terrible place

indicators.note: the answer sits in the run of clue letters spanning the three words

explanation.surface: A diner in a newly opened café finds it a dreadful spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'cafE-A TERrible'; 'a new' and 'place' are surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: An eater is anyone consuming food, such as a diner at a table.

clue.text: Stand for heartless rogue getting handout

indicators.note: taking away the heart of the word rogue leaves only its first and last letters

parts.note: a present is a gift, something handed out

explanation.surface: Someone stands up to a cruel villain who is given charity.
explanation.definitionFit: To represent something is to symbolise it or act on its behalf.

clue.text: Reason for arranging in order make-up etc

parts.note: to tell someone to do something is to order them

indicators.note: make-up as a verb, to make up, reworks the letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Explanation of why cosmetics and so on are put in a set order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make-up' rearranges ETC into ECT; 'for arranging' is surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Intellect is the faculty of reasoning and understanding.

clue.text: Cutting of rent doubtful — give voice!

indicators.note: doubtful suggests the word rent is uncertain and so is rearranged

parts.note: to chant is to sing or speak out rhythmically

explanation.surface: A tenant unsure about the rent is told to speak up.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant means incisive and sharp, as a cutting remark is.

clue.text: To go after a bit would be the end!

parts.note: to tail someone is to follow them
a piece is a bit

explanation.surface: Chasing a small portion would be the final straw.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailpiece is a final section or ending, as a decoration at a chapter's close.

clue.text: Having managed to occupy most in retirement, beam

indicators.note: the word for managed occupies, so sits inside, the other piece
in retirement means drawn back, so the word most is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before turning
ran is managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: Having succeeded in filling most of one's retirement, someone smiles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retirement' turns MOST into TSOM, and RAN goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A transom is a horizontal crossbar, as above a door or window.

clue.text: A second pressing

explanation.surface: A moment of pushing down.
explanation.definitionFit: An instant is a moment of time, and instant also means urgent or immediate, as a pressing need is.

clue.text: Seating to set in the sun

indicators.note: set in means placed inside, putting one piece within another

parts.note: Sol is the sun, from the Latin

explanation.surface: Chairs arranged to sit out in sunshine.
explanation.definitionFit: A stool is a backless seat, a piece of seating furniture.

clue.text: View taken of a vegetable with oily stuffing

indicators.note: the oily word is stuffed into the vegetable, so placed inside it

parts.note: an onion is a vegetable
oily can mean unctuous, and pi is slang for sanctimonious or smugly pious

explanation.surface: Someone forms a judgement on a vegetable filled with something greasy.
explanation.walkthrough: PI is old slang for pious; 'oily' in its unctuous sense stands in for it.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion is a view or judgement someone holds.

clue.text: Model girl — the slimmer

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so these letters are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A fashion model is the thinnest of the group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' rearranges GIRL THE; it looks like a noun describing the girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Lighter means weighing less, as someone thinner does.

clue.text: The path trodden by those forming a union

definitions.text: The path trodden by those forming a union

parts.words: The path trodden by those forming a union
parts.note: the union is a marriage, and the path is the one walked in church at a wedding

explanation.surface: The route walked by people founding a trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride walks down the passage between pews of a church to be married.

clue.text: Brooking no opposition when in office?

definitions.text: Brooking no opposition when in office?

parts.words: Brooking no opposition when in office?
parts.note: suggests a domineering ruler in power, but also a boss reading letters aloud to a secretary at work

explanation.surface: A leader in government who tolerates no dissent.
explanation.definitionFit: Dictating means ordering people about, and also speaking words for a typist to take down.

clue.text: Outsized, English Doctor of Divinity went out and took medicine

indicators.note: the doctor's letters go outside the other pieces, wrapping round them

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: A large English clergyman left and took his pills.
explanation.definitionFit: To dose is to take or give a measured amount of a drug.

clue.text: The Greek character imprisoned by critical Pharisees

indicators.note: the answer is locked up inside the letters of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A Greek figure jailed by censorious religious leaders.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha is the first letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Do they raise the roof with their harsh criticisms!

definitions.text: Do they raise the roof with their harsh criticisms!

parts.words: Do they raise the roof with their harsh criticisms!
parts.note: raising the roof reads as making an uproar, but the workers literally put roofs up, and slating is harsh criticism

explanation.surface: Fierce critics cause a loud commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaters are roofers who lay slates, and those who slate, meaning criticise severely.

clue.text: Designate a quiet period

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
point and period both mean a full stop

explanation.surface: Name a calm spell.
explanation.definitionFit: To appoint someone is to name or assign them to a role.

clue.text: Slough is without an art gallery — that must be changed!

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the bog word wraps round the gallery

parts.note: a slough is a muddy bog or swamp
the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: Slough, the English town, lacks a gallery and ought to improve.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough poses as the town west of London; here it is a muddy swamp. The TATE is London's best-known gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutated means altered in form or nature.

clue.text: Suite taken ahead of Her Majesty has a coach

indicators.note: the suite word is put in front of the queen's letters

parts.note: a train is a retinue or suite of attendants
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: The Queen's entourage goes in front, with a carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suite' looks like rooms, but means a train of followers; 'coach' looks like a carriage, but is a sports instructor.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainer is someone who coaches athletes.
